newsitem.title: USA: Fed should act early on inflation - Boskin.
newsitem.headline: Fed should act early on inflation - Boskin.

text.p: The Federal Reserve should be poised to take some pre-emptive action if signs of inflation start to appear, a top economist said Friday.

Speaking at a securities industry conference, Michael Boskin, chairman of the Consumer Price Index Commission, said the Fed should act once it sees the early signs that "the preconditions of inflation are on us."

"The Fed will need to take pre-emptive action," Boskin, who was chief White House economist under President Bush, told the conference. He said that by acting before inflation hits, the Fed would have time to make a difference in the marketplace.

Boskin, a Tully M. Friedman professor of economics and senior fellow of the Hoover Institute at Stanford University, warned about the threats abroad to the current inflation level, citing Japan and Europe as possible problem countries.

"I worry about the possibility that Europe and Japan ... may finally get their act together," he said. Boskin said the two countries have been "flat on their back" for some time and that a recovery could be in the making.
